limitations.effect: The tests establish state-machine behavior, not performance or availability under a distributed runtime.
limitations.statement: The reproduction is an in-memory deterministic reference model, not a production storage engine.

limitations.effect: A production implementation still needs a database transaction, compare-and-set, or equivalent linearizable boundary.
limitations.statement: A Python RLock models atomicity only inside one process.

limitations.effect: The max-observed-token fixture intentionally demonstrates this gap rather than claiming to repair it.
limitations.statement: A sink with no authoritative ownership lookup cannot know about a transfer until it observes a newer token.

limitations.effect: Wall-clock expiry, network delay distributions and provider interruption are outside this fixture.
limitations.statement: No timing assumptions, network services or external side effects are exercised.

limitations.effect: The model requires one fence domain per protected resource or an explicitly comparable global domain.
limitations.statement: Tokens from unrelated allocators are not necessarily comparable.

limitations.effect: The capsule's schema hash remains valid at its registration commit, while the dispatch-base schema has a different additive-hardening hash.
limitations.statement: The task capsule records historical source bytes; it is not a claim that every source stayed unchanged through dispatch.

limitations.effect: The requested reasoning label cannot be confirmed as the executing runtime setting.
limitations.statement: Machine evidence reports model gpt-5.6-sol-max-fast; it does not expose an xhigh reasoning field.
